title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 16-18): Grothendieck is classifying conformal surfaces with boundary through their complex double. A connected bordered conformal surface X with nonempty boundary is treated as a pair (𝔛, σ): 𝔛 is a connected Riemann surface, σ is an antiholomorphic involution with nonempty fixed locus, and X = 𝔛/σ with ∂X = image of 𝔛^σ. The question is when X carries a unique 'distinguished' (canonical constant-curvature) metric. The problem cases are those where 𝔛 is not hyperbolic: 𝔛 = ℂ or 𝔛 = ℙ¹. This page finishes the case 𝔛 = ℂ.

(1) Antiholomorphic involutions of ℂ. Any antiautomorphism has the form z ↦ a z̄ + b. Requiring it to be an involution forces |a| = 1 and a b̄ + b = 0. Such a map always has fixed points, because glide reflections are not involutions. So every antiholomorphic involution of ℂ is the orthogonal reflection in some real affine line, not necessarily through the origin. The previous page normalised to lines through 0.

(2) The quotient X = ℂ/σ is therefore conformally a closed half-plane, with its boundary.

(3) Metrics. The flat metrics c|dz|² are quasi-invariant under the whole conformal group: affine maps multiply them by a constant. They are genuinely invariant under all finite-order automorphisms, in particular under σ. They therefore descend to X. So X carries a one-parameter family (a 'droite', really a ray) of distinguished flat Riemannian metrics, unique up to a constant.

(4) NB. The standard model is the closed upper half-plane H̄ = {Im z ≥ 0}. Its automorphism group is identified with the group of affine automorphisms of ℂ commuting with z ↦ z̄, which Grothendieck calls the real affine group. The next page records the outcome: for X ≅ ℂ or H̄ the distinguished metrics form one class modulo constants, a single Aut X-orbit. For ℙ¹ or the disc they form 3- resp. 2-parameter families, again single orbits.
errors: Minor imprecision: affine maps z ↦ az + b with a, b real all commute with conjugation. But only those with a > 0 preserve H̄; a < 0 exchanges the upper and lower half-planes. So Aut(H̄) is the identity component Aff⁺(ℝ), not the full real affine group. (Möbius maps in PSL₂(ℝ) that move ∞ are excluded because they do not preserve the boundary line ℝ.)
'une droite de métriques' should read as a ray (positive multiples c|dz|², c > 0), i.e. one metric modulo constants. The next page states it correctly ('classe de métriques mod constantes').

ideas.what: Bordered Riemann surface as a quotient of its double by an antiholomorphic involution with fixed points
ideas.modern_name: Schottky double / real Riemann surfaces (Klein surfaces)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (real/bordered curves and Teichmüller towers); not developed there

ideas.what: Classification of antiholomorphic involutions of ℂ as reflections in real lines
ideas.modern_name: Real structures on the affine line

ideas.what: Canonical flat metric on the closed half-plane, unique up to scale, forming one orbit under Aut
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization of simply connected bordered surfaces / canonical constant-curvature metrics

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine case analysis (𝔛 = ℂ) inside a classification of bordered conformal surfaces admitting canonical metrics. It is mathematically standard and serves as groundwork for the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' project. Nothing here is new.
